display.title: Shavuos Flowers and Dairy Foods: Why We Eat Milchigs
display.summary_short: Why shuls are decorated with flowers on Shavuos, why we eat dairy foods like cheese blintzes, and why every Yom Tov must be filled with joy.
display.summary_long: A short Shavuos talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given just after the holiday. Uncle Yossi recalls hearing the Ten Commandments in shul and the colorful flowers that decorate the shul and the home, a reminder of the flowers that covered Har Sinai when the Torah was given. He explains one reason for eating dairy foods such as cheese blintzes: once the Jewish people received the laws of kashrus at Har Sinai, they could not eat meat until they had learned to prepare it properly, so they ate dairy. Every Shavuos we remember this. Like every Yom Tov, Shavuos is a time of joy, as the Torah commands, and the clip ends as Uncle Yossi announces the return of music after the days of Sefirah.
display.lesson: Shavuos customs remind us of receiving the Torah at Har Sinai, and every Yom Tov is a time to be truly joyful.
